Odia Festival Calendar

Every Odia festival in your Google Calendar. Free, and it keeps itself up to date.

  • Raja Parba

Add to Google Calendar
Add on iPhone Share

You need to be signed in to your Google account.

How to add it

  1. Tap Add to Google Calendar above.
  2. Google Calendar opens. Tap Add.
  3. Done. In a few minutes the festivals appear in your phone’s calendar and widget, in Odia. Tap one to see its details.
Having trouble on your phone?

If nothing happens when you tap the button, open your browser’s ⋮ menu, choose Desktop site, and tap the button again.

If the festivals still don’t show on your phone, open the Google Calendar app → ☰ → Settings → Odia Festivals and turn on Sync.

Set reminders

Get a notification a week before, 3 days before, the day before, and on the day of each festival.

  1. Open the Google Calendar app → ☰ (top left) → Settings.
  2. Choose Odia Festivals.
  3. Under the all-day notifications option, add the ones you want:
    1 week before 3 days before The day before On the day

If one isn’t listed, choose Custom and enter the number of days. This only affects the festival calendar, not your other events.

Questions

Is it free?

Yes, completely. There’s nothing to install.

Will I get emails or invitations?

No. Nothing is ever sent to you. The festivals appear only because you added the calendar yourself.

Can anyone see my calendar or details?

No. You only see the festival list. Your own calendar, email and name aren’t shared with anyone.

What about next year’s festivals and corrected dates?

They update automatically. You don’t need to add the calendar again.

Where do the dates come from?

The Shree Jagannath Temple Administration’s festival calendar, the Government of Odisha holiday notification, and the Kohinoor Panjika. Dates not yet confirmed say so in the event details and are corrected when the official calendars come out.

How do I remove it?

On a computer or in a browser, open calendar.google.com → Settings → Odia Festivals → Unsubscribe.

Found a wrong date?

Tell us here, and mention which panjika or calendar has the correct date.
